For input 1, I'm sketching an 8x10 grid with color 3, axis row 1, and a triangle-wave motif occupying the upper half, touching the left edge—trying a few variations on where the wave bumps land before settling on something with wrap_edge behavior on the right side instead.

I want a clearer motif than plain dashes, so I'm planning to test three separate inputs and check their visual output: input 1 as an 8x10 grid with color 3 and a period-4 zigzag in the upper half touching the right edge, then move to designing input 2 as a larger zigzag variant with a different color.

I'll mirror the example structure for input2, shifting the motif so the axis row touches the right edge instead of the left, keeping the same color and row pattern. For input3, I'm setting up an 8x10 grid with color 6 in the lower half, axis at row 6 touching the left edge, and starting with a simpler motif spanning all columns in that row.

I'm working out the periodic pattern with period 3: row6 gets columns where x%3 is 0 or 2, and row5 gets the column where x%3 equals 1, checking that c=2 maps correctly to x=7 giving row5 placement — this checks out, so the extent spans columns 0 through 4.
